title: Sparse LU obstruction conjecture
statement:
A matrix is **sparse** when its relevant rows and columns have uniformly boundedly many nonzero entries. A sparse LU decomposition is a factorization

$$
\partial=PLUQ
$$

where $P$ and $Q$ are permutation matrices and $L$ and $U$ are sparse lower- and upper-triangular matrices. **Sparse LU obstruction conjecture.** There exist sparse matrices with no sparse LU decomposition. Moreover, with high probability, a uniformly random sparse matrix has no sparse LU decomposition. Such a decomposition would give a sparse lift with determinant $1$ and hence avoid torsion in the corresponding full-rank one-complex; the existence of sparse LU decompositions is left open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.02249

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).
source_name: Michael Freedman and Matthew B. Hastings, “Building manifolds from quantum codes”, arXiv:2012.02249 (2021).
